subject: Result interpretation when using a random slope across a region for covariates in inla

messages.author: 19a17897bcd210d4
messages.subject: Result interpretation when using a random slope across a region for covariates in inla
parts:
Hi all,

I'm now studying the spaial variation in the effects of air pollution on human health. I want to know if the effects of air pollutants, e.g., pm10, vary spatially within a region.

Follow the book "Saptial and Spatial-temporal Bayesian Models with R-INLA" (page 192), I found the code: formula.inla1<- RESP~ f (ID.PM10, PM10, model="iid", graph=torino.adj, constr=TRUE, hyper=list(prec=list(prior="gaussian,param=c(0,1))))+f(ID.MUNICIPALITY, model="besag",graph=torino.adj)

mod.zib1<-inla(formula.inla1,family="zeroinflated.binomial.0",Ntrials=TotalPop,data=data,control.compute=list(dic=TRUE))

I used the code to derive the estiamtes for PM10 effects across the region：mod.zib1$summary.random$ID.PM10

But how to describe or explain the results?

I know how to interpret the result when using the code: formula.inla1<- RESP~ PM10+f(ID.MUNICIPALITY, model="besag",graph=torino.adj)

the exp(β) estimate for PM10 implies the risk increase associated with per one unit increase in PM10 concentration.

Thanks heaps for any help.

messages.author: 66ed4f72a898a51c
messages.subject: Re: Result interpretation when using a random slope across a region for covariates in inla
parts:
I think is better to change it in one of the two ways bellow

1. use constr=FALSE in 

RESP~ f(ID.PM10, PM10, model="iid", graph=torino.adj, constr=FALSE, ...

2. add the overall coefficient
RESP~ PM10 + f(ID.PM10, PM10, model="iid", graph=torino.adj, constr=TRUE, ...

The first gives a regression coefficient for each area. The interpretation is as usual, just depending on the link function used for the linear predictor.

The second option gives an overall regression coefficient and an additional for each area. This additional one gives the specific increase/decrease on the effect at each area.

best regards,
Elias
